name: 'Art in Every Day Life' Heritage Trail
description: Walk along new heritage trail exploring the lost heritage of Gilbert Bayes' 'Art in Everyday Life' sculptures scattered across the St Pancras Housing Estates.

name: 1.20 Oxo Tower Wharf
description: Carreducker bespoke shoemakers and Shoe & Leather School is located at Unit 1.20, one of 25 workshop and retail units in Oxo Tower Wharf. It overlooks the courtyard towards the Bargehouse building from the first floor walkway and is a multi-purpose space used as a workshop, showroom and teaching space.
address: Unit 1.20, The Courtyard, Oxo Tower Wharf, SE1 9PH

name: 10 Downing Street
description: 10 Downing Street has been the residence of British Prime Ministers since 1735. Behind its famous black door the most important decisions affecting Britain for nearly 300 years have been taken.

name: 11 Hungerford Road
description: Victorian Tardis. The original house dates from 1864, but was completely redeveloped in 1984 and fine tuned in 1993 and in 2023 by three different architects. Double height and open interiors contrast with a Victorian facade. Tea, coffee and cakes with all funds raised to go to Shelter will be on sale all day. . Cash only @ £5 per drink and cake.

name: 2 Belgrave Road: Victorian house with Luis Barragán inspired interior
description:
A Luis Barragán inspired design for the interior of a typical late Victorian house in East London. 
The use of bold vivid colour banishes the sterility that can accompany modernism without the loss of its hallmark simplicity and elegant line. This approach can be accommodated within houses whose external architecture has a very different heritage. Its achievement does not require a big budget

name: 31 Milton Road
description:
A three-storey Victorian house was split into flats in the 1970s.  The current owners have turned it back into single family home, with a large open-plan ground floor, professional kitche and Mediterranean garden, revealing long-hidden Victorian features in the process.
Last year the loft was converted into an airy master bedroom and en suite with views of both sunrise and sunset.
address: 31 Milton Rd , Churchfield Village, Acton, W3 6QA

name: 6 Wood Lane
description: A double-height ark floats above a masonry base & entrance footbridge.  Off the elevated living area a smokers' balcony overlooks the lush garden below. Above, semi circular terrace and winter garden nestle within the wooded surrounds.

name: 9 Wavell Court, Croydon
description: Wavell Court is a 1975 terrace of 17 houses, with each plot only 3.7m wide. The original designers ambitiously attempted to squeeze all the components of a functional 3-storey family home into the minimal possible width. No. 9 has been sensitvely restored to an appropriate mid-century style by the two architects who live there.
address: 9 Wavell Court, 9 Elgin Road, Croydon, CR0 6XB

name: A Ruskinian Walk Through Shared Heritage
description: Ruskinian walk from RIBA award-winning Chiswick Business Park, Gunnersbury Triangle Nature Reserve through South Acton Estate, birthplace of artist Patrick Caulfield; Woodlands Park Ice House; to home of William Willett, initiator of Daylight Saving Time.
address: Building 3, Chiswick Business Park, 566 Chiswick High Road, W4 5YA

name: Air Raid Shelter, St Leonards Court
description: The Air Raid Shelter was first built in 1939 for the the residents of St Leonards Court. A dormitory annex with 48 beds was added in 1940.  Some of the original features, such as handmade lampshades, are remarkably well preserved.

name: Alexandra Road Estate Flat 85B (Rowley Way)
description: Visit a recently refurbished apartment of Neave Brown’s Alexandra Road Estate in Camden. This is a 3 bed maisonette flat, lower ground and ground floor levels on block B along the pedestrian Rowley Way.

name: All Saints Carshalton
description: 12C south aisle and former chancel. Blomfield nave, chancel, baptistry. Kempe glass, Bodley reredos and screen, spectacular Comper decorations, monuments and brasses, award-winning lighting scheme, fine modern benches.

name: All Saints Church, Edmonton
description: Listed Grade ll* and celebrating its 890th year, All Saints Church  has aspects of the fabric dating back to at least early C12 with further modification and additions in the 15th, 17th and 19th centuries.  Charles and Mary Lamb lived on Church Street, where the church is situated and are buried in the Garden of Remembrance within the churchyard.
address: All Saints Church, Church Street, N9 9AT

name: Argentine Ambassador's Residence
description: During the Open House Festival people will have the unique opportunity to explore the historic mansion.  Opening its doors on this special occasion, visitors will enjoy unprecedented access to the Argentine Ambassador's Residence in the UK and explore a glimpse of our culture through an art exposition of different Argentine artists.

name: Avery Hill Winter Garden
description: The Avery Hill Winter Garden is a remarkable Victorian glasshouse set within the historic Avery Hill estate in southeast London. Built in the late 19th century, it was once home to an extensive collection of exotic plants and remains one of London’s largest surviving Victorian winter gardens.

name: Barbican Conservatory
description: Join us to explore the architectural history and future of the City of London's iconic glasshouse. Hear from the team behind Barbican Renewal, who will be restoring and revitalising the Conservatory from 2027-2030 with improvements to accessibility, sustainability and a new plant collection. Take part in a plant adoption event, leaving with a cutting from the Conservatory to grow at home.

name: Benjamin Franklin House
description:
Just steps from Trafalgar Square, is Benjamin Franklin House, the world's only remaining Franklin home.

For nearly sixteen years between 1757 and 1775, Benjamin Franklin – scientist, diplomat, philosopher, inventor, and Founding Father of the United States – lived behind its doors.

Built circa 1730, we are a Grade I listed house, with largely original flooring and wall paneling.

name: Bishops Palace and Park, Bromley (formerly Bromley Civic Centre).
description: The Bishop's Palace was the official residence of the Bishops of Rochester. The present building dates from 1775, although there have been manor houses on the site since the 10C. The estate was acquired by Victorian coal merchant Coles Child who undertook numerous alterations and additions designed possibly by Norman Shaw.  The Park contains St Blaise's Well, fernery, Ice House and the former moat
address: Bromley Palace Park, Adjacent to No 12 Rochester Avenue, Bromley

name: Boston Manor House
description: Boston Manor House is a Jacobean House built for Lady Mary Reade in 1623 and later owned by the Clitherow family from the 1670s until the 1920s. The House is now open to the public with free entry six days a week. Its beautifully restored historic interiors, including breath-taking ornate plasterwork, are joined by two community exhibition galleries, meeting rooms and an attractive modern café.
address: Boston Manor House, Boston Manor Road, Brentford, TW8 9JX

name: Brentford's Great West Road Centenary walking tour
description: The A4 Great West Road was 100-years-old in 2025. In 1933 J. B. Priestley wrote that: "Being new, the Great West Road did not look English. We might have suddenly rolled into California." Participants will see some of what remains of this unique corridor of Art Deco architecture and hear about some of the, famous, lost buildings of the inter war era.
address: The Market Place, corner of 194 High Street ( Dexters Estate Agents)

name: British Cardiovascular Society
description: 9 Fitzroy Square is the home of the British Cardiovascular Society. In addition to original architectural features, visitors will be able to view the BCS collection of objects illustrating the history of cardiology. Last entry 3.30 pm.
address: British Cardiovascular Society, 9 Fitzroy Square, W1T 5HW

name: Brixton Windmill
description: A wonderful reminder of Brixton's rural past and inner London's last working mill. Built in 1816 by the Ashby family who produced flour until 1934.  Restored to working order 2011. Producing flour today thanks to our volunteer millers.

name: Brockwell Hall
description: Brockwell Hall was originally built in 1811-1813 for a wealthy Ludgate Hill glass maker as the centrepiece of his estate. It has recently been restored by PRS Architects, following an initiative led by Brockwell Hall Community Partners. Original features of the Grade II* listed Recency Villa have been restored and new spaces inside the Hall created for park users and the local community to enjoy.

name: Bruce Castle Museum
description: Tudor Manor House built for Sir William Compton in 1514, substantially altered in 17C, 18C & 19C. A museum since 1906 housing local history and community collections, archives, art & exhibitions of Bruce Castle, and Haringey area.

name: Brutalism & High-Tech Architecture Tour
description: A guided architecture walk exploring London’s post-war transformation, from the Brutalist vision of the Barbican to the High-tech Lloyd's Building and contemporary towers of the City. Through key landmarks, the tour reveals how social ideals, technological innovation, and economic change have shaped the modern skyline.
address: north side of St Giles Cripplegate, close to Fore Street

name: Burgh House
description: Built in 1704 and 1720, Burgh House is a Grade I Listed Queen Anne and early Georgian house situated in the heart of Hampstead Village. As an independent charity, it serves as a cultural hub bringing together heritage, art and community programming. Burgh House is also an Arts Council England accredited museum with a collection relating to Burgh House and the local area.

name: Burton Mausoleum
description:
Grade II* listed mausoleum in the form of a Bedouin tent carved to resemble draping canvas. The mausoleum houses the coffins of Sir Richard and Lady Isabel Burton. The interior is painted with religious imagery and decorated with camel bells, lamps, and wreaths of flowers. 

Last entry: 3:30pm.
address: St Mary Magdalen's RC Church, 61 North Worple Way, Mortlake, SW14 8PR

name: Carshalton Water Tower and Historic Gardens
description: Early 18C Grade II listed building incorporating plunge bath with Delft tiles, orangery, saloon and pump chamber with part-restored water wheel. Hermitage and sham bridge in grounds.

name: Central Gurdwara (Khalsa Jatha) London
description: Central Gurdwara (Khalsa Jatha) London is the UK's oldest established Sikh Place of Worship. Originally founded in 1908 it has been at the current site since 1969 and has recently been refurbished into a modern Sikh place of worship.

name: Chelsea Physic Garden
description: Part of the Chelsea Heritage Quarter, Chelsea Physic Garden was established in 1673, by the Worshipful Society of Apothecaries of London.  This four-acre green space in the heart of Chelsea is London's oldest botanical garden and home to over 4,500 medicinal, edible and useful plants.
address: Chelsea Physic Garden, 66 Royal Hospital Road, SW3 4HS

name: City Hall
description: The sustainable headquarters of the Mayor of London and London Assembly located in the Royal Docks, Newham. The docks are re-emerging as a commercial and cultural hub, and an exciting new waterfront.

name: City Information Centre
description: London's main tourist information centre is clad in a specially manufactured system of 220 pre-finished stainless steel panels. The subtly reflective surface provides a striking counterpoint to St Paul's.

name: College of Optometrists
description: HQ of professional and examining body for UK optometrists occupying two terraced houses, No. 41 (Flitcroft c1730 with later additions) and No. 42 (rebuilt by Tarmac plc, c1989 with rear extension over the former back yard) including Council Chamber, Georgian-style print room, modern meeting spaces, recording studio, academic library and refurbished museum.

name: Cranford Park - Stables and Secret Garden
description: Discover the hidden history of Cranford Park at this special open day. Explore the beautifully restored Grade II listed 18th-century stables and the secluded Secret Garden, once the estate's kitchen courtyard. Learn how these surviving buildings reveal life behind the scenes of the lost Cranford House estate and the ongoing conservation of this remarkable historic landscape.
address: Cranford Park, The Parkway, Hounslow, TW5 9RZ

name: Crown Court Church of Scotland
description: A Church of Scotland in London, home to the longest-established Presbyterian congregation in London, worshipping in this location in Covent Garden since 1719. The current building is red brick with Portland stone dressings in a restrained, finely crafted Free Style. Three storeys, recessed slated attic, mullioned and transomed windows. Fine stained glass, most of which is by Farrar Bell.

name: Croydon Curiosity Rover
description: As part of Open House 2026 in Croydon, visit an exhibition of our summer programme with Creative Quests: Curiosity Rover, and try some creative missions of your own! Part art studio, part community hub and part roaming spacecraft, collect quests to explore Croydon through noticing, movement, nature and imagination.

name: Croydon Minster
description: Medieval style church rebuilt by Sir George Gilbert Scott after 1867 fire. Tower & south porch are 15C. Large nave with open timber-work roof leads to chancel dominated by superb stained glass window & rich alabaster reredos.

name: Croydon Urban Room
description: The Croydon Urban Room is a space to talk about the past, present and future of the Croydon town centre. Through conversa­tions, stories, exhibitions and events, the Urban Room brings together the views of those who live, work and visit the area to create a shared vision of the future and test new uses live in action.

name: Crystal Palace Park Dinosaurs  – a tour with a London Blue Badge Tourist Guide
description:
Explore the world's first dinosaur models hidden in a south London park. The 30 Grade I listed, life-size statues of dinosaurs and other extinct animals at Crystal Palace Park have thrilled
visitors for 166 years. Tour is kids friendly.
address: Crystal Palace Overground station, Crystal Palace Overground station

name: Devonport Mausoleum
description: Beautiful mausoleum in former Royal Navy cemetery, restored 1999 by the University of Greenwich. Many interesting plaques and gravestones.

name: Dorich House Museum
description: Dorich House is the former studio home of the sculptor Dora Gordine and her husband the Hon. Richard Hare, a scholar of Russian art and literature. Now Grade II listed, the building was completed in 1936, to Gordine’s design, and is an exceptional example of a modern studio house by a woman artist.
address: Dorich House Museum, 67 Kingston Vale, SW15 3RN

name: Dr Johnson's House
description: Fine example of an early 5-floor Queen Anne town house with original panelling, open staircase and unique 'swinging panels' on the open-plan first floor. Johnson compiled his famous 'Dictionary of the English Language' (1755)  here.

name: Drapers' Hall
description: Livery hall first built in the 1530s, twice destroyed by fire and rebuilt (1666 & 1772). Late 19C facade and opulent Victorian interior.

name: Drink, respectability and resistance
description: This guided walking tour explores the social history of Tottenham — centred around Bruce Castle Park, Bruce Grove and Tottenham High Road — through three interconnected themes: drink, respectability and resistance. It examines how everyday spaces such as streets, homes, pubs and civic buildings were shaped by competing ideas about behaviour, morality and control.
address: Bruce Castle Museum, Lordship Lane, N17 8NU

name: Eastbury Manor House
description: One of the finest surviving Elizabethan red brick Manor houses- Grade I listed. Contains 17th Century wall-paintings, charming walled garden and a fine Tudor tower with original stairs. Many original features have been restored and layout remains mostly unchanged in over 400 years.
address: Eastbury Manor House, Eastbury Square, Barking, IG11 9SN

name: Eastcote Walking Tour
description: Discover the fascinating history of Eastcote and its surroundings, focused on how the landscape has changed, from the exclusively agricultural area to the today's modern suburb, revealing some of the oldest local buildings and their stories
address: Eastcote Station, Field End Road, Pinner, HA5 1QZ

name: Eco Punk
description: Eco Punk consists of a generous rear extension plus the remodel of an Edwardian house located in a conservation area. The new layout unlocks the spatial potentials. Besides beautifully crafted lounges, dining and utility areas, there is a kitchen that forms the centre piece. The latter is designed for a professional chef. An elegant, natural material palette ties the scheme together.

name: Emery Walker's House
description: The home of Emery Walker, printer, antiquary and mentor to William Morris. A unique Arts and Crafts domestic interior.

name: Estorick Collection of Modern Italian Art
description: The Estorick Collection is housed in a beautiful Georgian building previously known as Northampton Lodge. Today, the museum comprises six galleries over three floors, as well as a library, offices, a café and bookshop.

name: Explore the authentically recreated Colony Room
description: A revival and love letter to London’s lost bohemia. Travel back in time to the legendary haunt of some of Soho's greatest creatives.   Featuring pictures, press cuttings and even the piano from the much loved private members club.

name: Fenton House and Garden
description: Beautiful town house retaining many original features and housing important decorative arts collections.  Surrounded by a walled garden.

name: Fitzrovia Chapel
description: Loughborough Pearson's red brick building is unimposing from the outside, but inside is a riot of Gothic Revival design. Golden mosaics reveal the character of the Grade II* listed chapel, built as part of the Middlesex Hospital.

name: Fitzroy Park Allotments
description: Open allotment site.

name: Former Carbonic Gas Works, 142 Lea Bridge Road
description:
Paradise works artist studios in the Old Carbonic Works that is thought to be the birthplace of commercial fizzy drinks in the late 18th Century. It features in the Lea Valley and Hackney Conservation area report found online.


https://hackney.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s68747/240220%20Appendix%20A%20Lea%20Bridge%20Conservation%20Area%20Appraisal.pdf
address: Paradise works, 142 Lea Bridge Road, E5 9RB

name: Former Edmonton Girls' Charity School
description: The former Charity School was constructed in 1793, by Obadiah Legrew, who also purchased the adjoining no.24 Church Street, part of the surviving earlier 18th century range, to create a small cottage for the School Mistress.
address: Charity School Hall (next door to 24 Church Street), N9 9DU

name: Foster + Partners
description: We're excited to open up our London campus. Foster + Partners is a global studio for sustainable architecture, urbanism, engineering and design, founded by Norman Foster in 1967. Hosted across several buildings, the public can explore the studio, take part in interactive exhibitions and workshops, and gain an insight into the wide range of disciplines and projects across the globe.

name: Garrick's Temple to Shakespeare
description: Grade I listed Georgian garden building. Tribute to Shakespeare built in the Ionic style by actor David Garrick. Arcadian Thames-side setting in restored 18C gardens thought to be by Capability Brown.

name: Gaunson Creative Open Studios part of Markfield Road Festival
description: Gaunson Creative Studios in South Tottenham, home to over 70 artist studios, will be opening its doors for the first time since 2019. Visitors will be able to meet and buy from over 50 artists across the weekend.
address: Gaunson Creative Studios, Gunson House, Markfield Road, N15 4QQ

name: Golden Lane Estate, tours, community centre and access to flats
description: Tours around Golden Lane Estate, access to the Community Centre and access to a number of flats
address: Golden Lane Community Centre, Fann Street, EC1Y 0SA

name: Good Shepherd Studios
description: The doors to the building will be opened to the public. Not only will visitors get the opportunity to see "behind the scenes" at Good Shepherd Studios but they will have the opportunity to join taster sessions from site regulars and find out more about what takes place onsite at Our Pastures Community Garden and Pastures Centre too.

name: Green Lodge
description: Green Lodge is a low-energy family home by Stylus Architects, carefully embedded into the landscape of Putney Heath. Much of the accommodation is concealed below ground, allowing the building to maintain a modest presence whilst bringing natural light into every room through a series of lightwells and rooflights.

name: Grove Gardens Chapel
description:
A small, charming Gothic Revival cemetery chapel in Richmond Old Burial Ground. Recently conserved and back in public use, Grove Gardens Chapel made from Kentish ragstone, with plate tracery and a mosaic altarpiece. It was deconsecrated in the 1960s and then restored for community use in the 1990s.

The Fixery, Richmond's new swap, repair, and reuse hub will also be operating on the open day.
address: Richmond Cemetery, Grove Gardens, Lower Grove Road, TW10 6HP

name: Hampstead Friends Meeting House
description: Listed Arts and Crafts freestyle building with plain interior and many charming original features, sympathetically modernised in 1991. Entrance via listed gateway.

name: Harfield Gardens House
description: Harfield Gardens is an award-winning renovation of a British modernist house on a constrained site. Originally single storey, planning permission was granted for a second storey to double the internal floor space. Huge floor-to-ceiling windows with sliding doors open the interiors to bamboo-lined courtyards, blurring the boundary between interior and exterior, a hallmark of midcentury design.

name: Herne Hill Velodrome
description:
Herne Hill Velodrome, opened in 1891, hosted track cycling events for the 1948 Olympics, is now home to a thriving grassroots cycling facility - hosting everything from Learn to Cycle to local and international racing events. 
HHV overcame the threat of closure in the early 2000s, and a new pavilion, designed by Mike Taylor of Hopkins Architects, opened in 2017.

name: Hidden ceilings & 300 years of secrets: SGTM Open Day
description: Climb a ladder into the roof space above one of London's best-kept secrets and come face to face with Hawksmoor's beautiful ceiling. Explore Teulon's dramatic architecture, uncover tales of radical thinkers, pioneering doctors and inventive writers, and lose yourself in one of the capital's most secret churches. The roof space tour will be bookable on the day and you'll need to sign a disclaimer.
address: St George the Martyr, 44 Queen's Square, WC1N 3AH

name: Highgate Literary & Scientific Institution
description: Fine stuccoed building overlooking Pond Square, and home to the Institution since 1840. Formed from 1790 coach house, stables and yard, with final additions c1880. Guided tours will be available.

name: Hogarth's House
description: Early 18th century red brick country home of artist William Hogarth, extended significantly c. 1749-1764. The 2020 extension, funded by the National Lottery Heritage Fund, added the new Weston Studio for learning and activities, and a curved glass wall in the shape of Hogarth's Line of Beauty. Delightful re-landscaped and reinterpreted walled garden containing famous ancient mulberry tree.
address: Hogarth Lane, Great West Road, W4 2QN

name: Holy Trinity Church Sloane Square
description: A sumptuous feast of Victorian stained glass & bold sacred sculpture in what Sir John Betjeman called the 'cathedral of the Arts and Crafts movement.' Work by William Morris, Edward Burne-Jones, William Blake- Richmond & Christopher Whall.
address: 146 Sloane Street (just off Sloane Square), SW1X 9BZ

name: House Mill
description: The World’s largest tidal mill. 5-storey, timber-framed, brick-clad timber watermill with four waterwheels, originally built in 1776 to mill grain for distillery trade. Operational until 1940. On historic 3 Mills Site, Clock Mill adjacent (No access) .
address: Three Mill Lane, Bromley by Bow , E3 3DU

name: Howard Hodgkin Studio
description: Sir Howard Hodgkin (1932 – 2017) was one of England’s most celebrated contemporary artists. Abstracted yet allusive, apparently spontaneous but in fact highly controlled, his paintings convey feeling through gesture and colour.  His former studio, converted from a nineteenth-century dairy, sits in the heart of Bloomsbury.
address: The Howard Hodgkin Studio, Address tbc to ticket holders, WC1 1AB

name: Ibraaz
description: Ibraaz is a London-based cultural institution for art,  culture and ideas from the Global Majority. Bringing together artists, thinkers, and communities through exhibitions, film, debate, publishing, and multidisciplinary programming, Ibraaz creates a brave space where culture fosters exchange, pluralism, and shared humanity.

name: In Situ: Croydon Space Station
description: Be inspired by Croydon's space age buildings and aviation history - from Apollo and Lunar House, to Croydon Airport. Build your own models of familiar buildings redesigned as spacecrafts and transform the town centre into a space station.

name: Inner Space Meditation Centre, Covent Garden
description: Inner Space, London’s oasis of calm, welcomes visitors back for the Open House Festival. Join us over two weekends for free Guided Meditations, Personal Development talks and inspiring wellbeing workshops that support and nurture mindfulness, resilience and inner balance. Take a moment to pause in our Quiet Room, a space that will leave you feeling reconnected, refreshed, uplifted, and renewed.

name: Inner Temple Gardens
description: Established by the Knights Templar in 1195, The Inner Temple has had a Gardener since 1307. Surviving The Great Fire of London, and the Blitz, the Gardens remain a secret and tranquil oasis. Today the Garden is managed for beauty and biodiversity, providing a haven for people and wildlife in the heart of the City.
address: The Inner Temple Gardens, Crown Office Row, EC4Y 7BS

name: International Maritime Organization
description: The International Maritime Organization is a specialized agency of the UN, responsible for the safety and security of shipping and the prevention of marine pollution by ships. It is the only UN organization with headquarters in London.

name: Kaymet Factory
description: The operational factory of Kaymet, a maker of trays and trolleys since 1947. A hidden 1950s building with a small yard, originally a printing works. It is brick built, with clear-storey glazing and tubular truss north-light main shed roof.

name: Keats House
description:
Keats House is the beautiful Regency villa, where Romantic poet John Keats found inspiration, friendship and love. Today, it is a museum provided by the City of London Corporation for the benefit of London and the nation.
Our current art exhibition, The Nightingale Suite, is inspired by the birdsong about which Keats wrote 'Ode to a Nightingale' when he was living at the House.

name: Kempton Steam Museum
description: 1920s water pumping station comprising of several architectural styles. Interior retains original steam pumping machinery and historic electrical equipment.
address: Kempton Park Pumping Station, Snakey Lane, TW13 6XH

name: Kenwood
description: A striking Neoclassical villa in tranquil gardens on Hampstead Heath, Kenwood boasts breath-taking interiors by Robert Adam and a world-class art collection.

name: Kew House
description: A family home renown for it's quality of space and light, set around a courtyard and formed from two gabled Corten steel buildings connected by a glazed link.  The basement gallery will be showing Art Form, an exhibition on the engineering of 50 major artworks by Price & Myers.

name: Kilmorey Mausoleum
description: Egyptian-style, pink and grey mausoleum created for the second Earl of Kilmorey and Priscilla Hoste. The form relates to the shrines at the heart of Egyptian Temples.
address: 275 St Margaret's Road (opposite Ailsa Tavern), TW1 1NJ

name: King's College London, The Maughan Library
description: London's first fireproof building, built to house records of the Court of Chancery. Now renovated to house a fine university library.

name: Kingston Historic walk
description:
We are running our usual guided walking tours around historic Kingston this year. Come and find out interesting facts and stories about old Kingston. You will be amazed about how much you learn and enjoy.



Our guided tours are informative, interesting and fun. For more information about us visit: https://www.kingstontourguides.org.uk/
address: Market house, Kingston upon Thames, KT1 1JX

name: Kingswood House
description: Grade II listed building owned by Southwark Council. Large, 19th century mansion built in the form of a stone-faced baronial castle for the inventor of Bovril. Interior includes substantial wood panelling and a great hall. The building is managed by HH KIngswood Ltd and is used as a cultural and community space.

name: Ladbroke Hall
description: Set in the historic Sunbeam Talbot factory, a 1903 Beaux Arts building in Ladbroke Grove, Ladbroke Hall perpetuates the building’s legacy of innovation and creation. A space for exploration, inspiration and connection, across the many forms of arts and creative expressions, its seasonal live cultural programming celebrates the best of arts, live events and food.

name: Lisson Grove Studios
description:
Lisson Grove Studios is a 1088m2 mixed use creative workspace hub providing permanent, affordable workspace for artists, designers, makers and small creative businesses.

The complex opened in February 2026 and includes 38 creative enterprise studios, a café, dance & rehearsal studio, 22 desk spaces, a meeting room, two phone booths and an exhibition space, arranged over 5 split level floors.
address: Arbeit Studios - Lisson Grove -, Daventry House, Lisson Grove,

name: Little Mouse Cheese Shop
description: Visit Little Mouse, an Edwardian shop in South Norwood with original wooden frontage and fascia that is now an artisan cheesemonger.

name: London Centre for Book Arts
description: Based in what was once the heart of east London's print industry, the London Centre for Book Arts is an artist-run, open-access studio offering education programmes for the community and affordable access to resources for artists and designers. Visit for tours of the studio, demos and displays.

name: London Open Form Pavilion of Air
description: A floating acoustic architecture, playfully reframing public space as an essential community engagement through sound & site mapping. Accessed by smartphone, headphones & echoes.xyz app, the Pavilion is located outside the Serpentine Gallery,. Drawing on Oskar & Zofia Hansen’s Open Form architectural concept it is one of 15 in a series including Venice, Berlin, Dublin, Bergen and Arctic Norway.

name: London Scottish House (London Scottish Regimental Headquarters)
description: A Grade 2 listed former Territorial Army Drill Hall  featuring restored elements of the original 1882 design. It has a triple height central hall with the restored wrought iron balconies and roofing.  Notable Neo-Georgian design brickwork. It is also unique in being the last ever military drill hall built in the UK.
address: London Scottish House, 95 Horseferry Road, Westminster, SW1P 2DX

name: London, adored and explored
description: On this journey into Soho and St Giles, I want to show the different ways London’s streets are alive with love in all its varied forms. Buildings are often said to be sympathetic or out of place, in keeping or a departure from their surroundings. This tour will explore how the built environment reflects the relationships we conduct with each other.
address: Meet: Shaftesbury Memorial Fountain, Piccadilly Circus, W1J 9HS

name: Longfield Hall
description: Longfield Hall was built by William Minet and completed in 1889. It was designed by architect George Hubbard. William Minet also built the library opposite the hall, St James the Apostle Church on Knatchbull Road and much of the housing which surrounds Myatt’s Fields Park. Sadly the original library building was destroyed by a bomb during the Second World War, while Longfield Hall was undamaged.

name: MATT + FIONA: Croydon Skyline
description: As part of the weekend event Build /  Play / Shape Croydon, MATT+FIONA will lead a collaborative cardboard-build activity inspired by landmarks from Croydon's skyline. Visitors of all ages can help create a large scale installation using pre-made silhouette templates and recycled materials, contributing to "Croydon of the Future, Drawing on the Past".

name: Manor House Gardens Ice House
description: Grade II listed ice well and underground chambers (1770) in Manor House Gardens park, which provided ice for nearby Manor House. Cited in 2002 Civic Trust Awards.

name: Mansion House
description:
The official residence of the Lord Mayor of the City of London, retaining its 18C character, with superb plasterwork and wood carving.

PLEASE NOTE due to enhanced security measures ID will be required on the day for entry and security screening will be in place.

name: Markfield Beam Engine and House
description: A masterpiece of Victorian engineering, Markfield Beam Engine provided a vital public health facility from 1855-1964.
address: Markfield Park, Markfield Road, South Tottenham, N15 4RB

name: Moravian Close
description: A former stable yard of Sir Thomas More's Chelsea estate, now an 18C Chapel, other buildings, and burial ground. Parts of the enclosing walls are Tudor in origin. Ernest and Mary Gillick enhanced the grounds in the 20C.

name: Mount Pleasant
description: A former Victorian workhouse that has been transformed through LB Camden's Community Investment Programme into a state of the art facility for 50 homeless people laid out around a beautiful suntrap courtyard.

name: National Army Museum
description: Part of the Chelsea Heritage Quarter, the National Army Museum covers the British Army’s role from the Civil Wars to the modern day. Find inspiration in the stories of our soldiers and how their service shapes our world. Founded by Royal Charter in 1960, the Museum has been on the Chelsea site since 1970. Come and find out who we are and why we are here! Free entry to all our galleries!

name: Norman Fisher Observatory
description:
The Norman Fisher Observatory is owned and run by Croydon Astronomical Society. 
Open for the public to visit on clear Saturday evenings from September through to April, we will welcome visitors on Sunday 13th September between 1pm & 4pm.
address: Waterhouse Lane, Off Hayes Lane, Kenley, CR8 5EP

name: Nunhead Cemetery
description: Nunhead Cemetery, a Grade II* listed Victorian burial ground, is one of London's Magnificent Seven cemeteries  and is of historic and ecological importance. Set on a hillside, its 52 acres of woodland provides a green breathing space offering peace and tranquillity.  Imposing tombs contrast with the tumbling headstones and carved angels peer through a covering of ivy. Visits to chapel and crypt.

name: Obra
description: Obra is Sordo Madaleno’s transdisciplinary laboratory, open library, and public living room, turning our London studio into a public-facing space for curiosity, testing, and dialogue. An addition to London's architectural landscape, Obra will host temporary exhibitions, events, and talks fostering exchange between the studio, the environments it works within, and the communities it engages.
address: Obra, Regent's Wharf - 10 All Saints Street, N1 9RL

name: Old Royal Naval College
description: Sir Christopher Wren's riverside masterpiece in Greenwich, built as the Royal Hospital for Seamen and begun in 1696 on the site of the Tudor Greenwich Palace. Occupied by the Royal Naval College from 1869 to 1998, it is now a premier historic, cultural and educational destination in the heart of the Maritime Greenwich UNESCO World Heritage Site.
address: Old Royal Naval College, Greenwich, SE10 9NN

name: Old Royal Naval College - King William Court
description: Wren-designed building completed under the direction of Hawksmoor and Vanbrugh, 1698-1712. Original wood panelling, refurbished by Dannatt Johnson in 2001 for University of Greenwich.
address: King William Court, 30 Park Row, SE10 9NN

name: Old Royal Naval College - Queen Anne Court
description: Wren and Hawksmoor building, completed 1749 when Thomas Ripley built the pavilions facing the river. Highlights include council boardroom, grand staircase and restored Portland stonework. Refurbished in 2000 for University of Greenwich.
address: Queen Anne Court , 30 Park Row, SE10 9NN

name: Old Royal Naval College - Queen Mary Court
description: Last major building on the site (1751). Original layout, timber panelling, barrel vaulting and Portland stone. Refurbished in 2000 by Dannatt Johnson for University of Greenwich.
address: Queen Mary Court, 30 Park Row, SE10 9NN

name: OmVed Gardens
description: Discover OmVed Gardens’ new buildings and landscape during London Open House  Festival. Piers Smerin’s Douglas‑fir frames and cedar cladding form pyramid silhouettes, with a kitchen crowned by a roof garden. Passive design, raised roofs and oasthouse‑style vents keep spaces airy. Paul Gazerwitz’s hillside paths weave woodland, meadow, veg plots, ponds and orchard into a green village.

name: Ongéan
description:
Ongéan Ecosystem : 
Art Studios, Gallery, Performance Space, Edible Garden & Kitchen. All built and designed with 99% Reclaimed Materials by artist Adam Ge-Saelis.
address: Ongéan, Park Mews, Croxted rd, SE24 9DB

name: Open House 18 Woolwich Road
description: 18 Woolwich Road is a listed building known as the "Lodge", and part of the Greenwich Royal Hospital the entrance gatehouse of the third cemetery now a public park the Pleasaunce. The building is now a house occupied by Artist Fran Cottell who has added an extraordinary history using the house for her own work. A glazed roof to the rear addition has been designed by Elden Croy Architect.

name: Our Yard at Clitterhouse Farm
description: Come and visit this grassroots community enterprise where old meets new in the form of the historic farm buildings alongside our crowdfunded cafe. Find out how some of these historic buildings have been saved and lovingly bought back into community use, and find out about our future plans.
address: Clitterhouse Playing Fields, Claremont Rd, NW2 1AP

name: Parish Church of St Andrew, Enfield
description: Grade ll Listed church, that has been much added to over the 800 years of its existence. We have  recently refurbished the organ which has a fine circa 1750s wooden organ case.  The Church has an eight-bell peal still in weekly use– the oldest bell dates from 1680.
address: The Market Place, Church Street, Enfield, EN2 6LL

name: Parish Church of St Mary The Virgin Lewisham
description:
The church was rebuilt in late 15th century with some of that still remaining to this day.							
During the festival there will be opportunity to self-guide or join a group tour which will include access to restricted areas such as the crypt and tower. These last about 30 min and will start on each hour with the last starting at 3 pm

name: People's Museum Somers Town
description:
A great little museum set in the Grade 2 listed Ossulston Estate - a prime example of pre-war Social housing - based on Karl Marz Hof in Vienna.
Open Tuesday to Saturday 10am-5pm, plus Sunday 13th 12am-4pm.

name: Petty France and its environs
description: Petty France is a short street with a long history. This walk will time travel from the medieval origins of Petty France through its sensational history to its present distinguished profile. We shall study Charles Holden's 1927 Grade 1 listed  London Underground HQ, upstaged in 1976 by Sir Basil Spence's 1976 brutalist monument to modernism,  and where the original Queen Anne house was born.

name: Pif-Paf: Right To Play
description: Right To Play is a celebration and a call to action to fight for our Right To Play. With bamboo den and structure building, Puppetry interaction, a "Long Table Mud Kitchen" play and a Run, Jump, Swing sculpture.

name: Polish Social and Cultural Association
description: Built 1972-74 in a part-brutalist style, POSK is the largest Polish Centre in Western Europe. It contains a theatre, the Polish Library, the Polish University Abroad, a Joseph Conrad collection, the Piłsudski Institute, Jazz Café with regular live concerts, art gallery, and art collection on public display.

name: Pollocks House of Cards and Paper Gardens
description:
Build a towering house of cards inspired by architects Charles and Ray Eames 1950s classic building toy- with  cards specially produced from Pollock's  vintage Toy Theatre scenery.  Create a 3D  paper garden to take home
Or join architect Ambrose Gillick to build  giant lightweight constructions.  Suitable for all .
address: Pollock's Toy Museum, unit 49 Whitgift Centre, CR0 1UQ

name: Power in the eye of the beholder: Strand drawing tour
description: This walking tour explores the different ways power and wealth is exemplified in architecture around the Strand. Inspired by the methods of Giovanni Battista Piranesi and his depiction of 'power' in his works, we will be doing sketches throughout the tour, studying different types of architectural components and ornamentation to help us imagine and compose our own impactful landscapes.
address: Upper terrace, Somerset House, Strand, WC2R 1LA

name: Pullman Court
description: Grade II* listed buildings, modern movement style with balcony walkways and period internal features.

name: Queer Britain
description: Queer Britain Museum is the UK’s national LGBTQ+ museum.    Housed in a converted Victorian building in the heart of the regenerated King’s Cross area, the galleries feature over 200 objects from over 100 years of queer history.   At Open House 2026, Queer Britain’s volunteer guides will give talks demonstrating the museum’s mission to reclaim, preserve and inspire LGBTQ+ history.

name: Quentin Blake Centre for Illustration - New River Head
description:
An industrial heritage site that was the hub of one of London’s first major pieces of urban infrastructure.
Its 18th and 19th century buildings have been restored by Tim Ronalds Architects to create the Quentin Blake Centre for Illustration which opened to the public on June 5th 2026.
address: Quentin Blake Centre for Illustration, Rear of 28 Amwell Street

name: Reform Club
description: Built as a Whig gentleman's club and inspired by Italian Renaissance palaces. Lobby leads to an enclosed colonnaded courtyard with complementary glazed roof and tessellated floor. Tunnelled staircase leads to upper floor.

name: Rhymes and Reasons: Exploring the City of London through nursery rhymes
description: This walking tour explores the City of London through the lens of nursery rhymes, using both well-known and lesser-known verses as a playful way into its architecture, communities and history. Rhymes such as 'London Bridge is Falling Down' and 'Oranges and Lemons' are rooted in real places and experiences. Along the way we will uncover some of the darker stories that may lie behind these innocent verses.
address: South East corner of Charterhouse Square, near Carthusian Street

name: Rio Cinema
description: Grade II listed Art Deco cinema with stalls and circle created in 1937 within the shell of an Edwardian cinema, retaining many original features. In 2017  a new auditorium was created in the basement space.

name: Romans in London walk
description: Absorb the fascinating history of ancient Londinium, visiting sites where the Romans lived, worked, and played.

name: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew - Herbarium
description: The Herbarium, Library, Art & Archives building houses a working scientific collection located on Kew Green. We are excited to publicly showcase, through guided tours, our complex of historic and modern buildings, housing almost seven million preserved botanical collections, together with one of the largest botanical library, art, and archive collections in the world.

name: Royal College of General Practitioners
description: Grade II* listed building. Restored in 2012 to showcase magnificent Edwardian faience tile work, mosaic floor and other historic features in transformed modern surroundings that now provide the headquarters of the RCGP.

name: Royal Hospital Chelsea, Home of the Chelsea Pensioners
description: Part of the Chelsea Heritage Quarter, the Royal Hospital Chelsea has housed the Chelsea Pensioners since 1692. Join a Pensioner‑led tour of our grounds exploring its history and architecture from Wren to Soane. Enjoy free access to the Soane Stable Yard, museum and café, and visit nearby CHQ partners—the National Army Museum and Chelsea Physic Garden which are a short walk from each other.

name: Rudolf Steiner House
description: Unique example of Expressionist architecture in London with sculptural staircase based on organic plant forms. Grade II listed. New café area and renovations in 2008. Refurbishment of theatre and foyer 2020.

name: Rufford Mews Apartment
description:
Home to RHS Chelsea Gold Medalists Mike McMahon and Jewlsy Mathews, this space showcases a decade of their handcrafted furniture and cabinetry. 
Their work, all made by their own hands, has received international acclaim featuring in BBC Gardeners' World (TV), The Modern House, The Observer, Dwell, Interior Design and IDEAT. Experience bespoke design in every meticulously crafted detail.

name: Saint Nectarios Greek Orthodox Church
description: A Victorian Gothic Revival church hidden within Battersea's Shaftesbury Park Estate. Built in 1901 by architect G.H. Fellowes Prynne, it served the growing community before becoming a vibrant hub for Orthodox worship. Now home to a beautiful collection of icons donated from across the Orthodox world, alongside beautiful stained glass and original architectural details.

name: Sands End Arts & Community Centre
description: Amongst the RIBA Stirling Prize shortlist 2022 sits Mæ Architect's Sands End Arts & Community Centre in Fulham. The centre consists of a single-storey building comprising bright, airy and flexible event spaces and a community café.

name: Scadbury Moated Manor
description: See the archaeological excavations and Tudor foundations at Scadbury Moated Manor - which still has its moat around it.
address: Scadbury Moated Manor, Perry Street, Chislehurst, BR7 6LN

name: Segmental House
description: Renovation and extension of a Grade 2 listed, five storey house by Dominic  McKenzie Architects. New rear extension constructed using bespoke brickwork. Lower ground floor lined with douglas fir panelling throughout. Bespoke kitchen and pantry. Upper ground floor sensitively remodelled by DMA. Rear garden by Kawauchi Rowe Garden Design. Interior design consultant (upper floors) Patrick O'Donnell.

name: Senate House
description: London’s tallest secular building when it opened as the HQ of the University of London and home to the Ministry of Information during WWII, this Grade II* listed landmark features Classicism and Art Deco elements.
address: University of London, Malet Street, WC1E 7HU

name: Sex in the City - a tour of Covent Garden's history
description: This is a walking tour that delves into the scandalous history of Covent Garden. This tour explores a time when the area served as London’s notorious red-light district, focusing on the lives of those forced into illicit trades or marginalized by the stringent moral laws of the day. The walk will share the stories of those who lived, worked and played in the area in days gone by.
address: Opposite Covent Garden Underground Station, WC2E 9JT

name: Southbank Printmakers
description:
We are a friendly artist run gallery in Wells Street offering affordable, handmade fine art prints with a broad range of subjects created using many different printmaking techniques.
We aim to encourage people who have never encountered art before to experience printmaking through our regular workshops.

name: Southlands Arts Centre
description: Explore Southlands Arts Centre and discover the history and architecture of this Grade II listed Queen Anne-style building. Admire its distinctive red-brick façade, elegant decorative detailing and historic interiors, and learn how this former private residence has evolved into a thriving community arts centre, celebrating Hillingdon's rich architectural and cultural heritage.
address: Southlands Arts Centre, 75, The Green, West Drayton, UB7 7PW

name: Spitalfields - stories of people
description: For hundreds of years, Spitalfields has been a place where those seeking safety, work, and community have settled.  They all leave their mark in streets buildings in an area rich in history and architectural interest.

name: St Augustine's Church
description: St. Augustine's, Kilburn affectionately known as 'The Cathedral of North London' was established in 1870. Fr. Kirkpatrick, the first Vicar, engaged John Loughborough Pearson as the architect with the result being what many consider one of his finest works. Externally in 1890 with the tower and spire it became the 2nd tallest building in London (now ecclesiastically 2nd to St. Paul's Cathedral).

name: St Augustine's Tower
description: Grade I listed, remaining tower of medieval parish church, with working late 16C clock. New exhibition of Hackney's history. Extensive views from roof. (Organised by Hackney Historic Buildings Trust).

name: St Barnabas Church
description: St Barnabas Church is a grade II* listed building with many Arts and Crafts designed features. Including some wonderful examples of stained glass.
address: St Barnabas Church, St Barnabas Road, Walthamstow, E17 8JZ

name: St Bernards estate and houses, Croydon
description: 21 houses, in 4 terraces, built by Swiss architects Atelier 5 for Wates within the wider Park Hill Estate, Croydon.  Living areas on the upper floor are approached through a garden court.  Bedrooms downstairs open onto a lower garden.  The houses are accessed via walkways and sit within mature communal gardens providing private and open living.  Pevsner wrote, 'a group with few equals in Britain'.
address: Meet: by OH banner, St Bernard's, Chichester Road, Croydon, CR0 5UL

name: St Bride's Church, Fleet Street
description: Wren designed building of 1675, interior lost in blitz of 1940, reopened 1957 with 'Wren inspired' interior
address: St Bride's Church, St Bride's Avenue, EC4Y 8AU

name: St George's Cathedral
description: A stunning cathedral in the heart of London. Discover the story of a forgotten masterpiece. Designed by Augustus Pugin and opened in 1848, the original cathedral was hailed as England's foremost Catholic church before an incendiary bomb devastated the building in 1941. Explore the history, architecture and legacy that shaped the Cathedral you see today—and discover its remarkable story.

name: St James's Piccadilly
description: St James's Piccadilly is a Grade I listed Christopher Wren church in the heart of the West End. Completed in 1684, and known as the Artists' Church, its interiors include historic works of art by Grinling Gibbons (reredos, organ case and font), postwar Classical interiors by Albert Richardson, and contemporary art by Che Lovelace honouring the 18th-century abolitionist Quobna Ottobah Cugoano.

name: St Margaret's Church, Lee
description:
The Church was built in 1839/41 as a white 'Hall-Church'. 
The 1870s Gothic Revivalism was overseen to a very high standard, by James Brooks and helped by 10 top craftsmen of the day. We also have a WWI Memorial by Violet Pinwill.
address: St Margarets Church, Lee Terrace, SE13 5DN

name: St Mark’s Church
description: A Grade 2-listed mid-Victorian parish church in the Gothic style,  built of Kentish ragstone with a slate roof.  Unique features include a panel of hand-made decorated tiles beyond the High Altar - probably Royal Doulton - and five noted stained glass windows, probably by Alfred Hemming.  The baptistery is also noteworthy, with its font and five murals of Biblical scenes, painted in oil on canvas.

name: St Mary & St Joseph Roman Catholic Church, Poplar
description: Grade II Listed.   Designed by Adrian Gilbert Scott.  Cruciform shape (120 feet by 120 feet) of steel girder and brick construction. Its Lantern tower – based on Ely Cathedral – is supported on parabolic arches 35 feet wide and 50 feet high.  The Stained Glass Windows were designed by John Wilson of Edinburgh and the Stations of the Cross  carved in Blue Horton Stone by Peter Watts.
address: St Mary & St Joseph Church, Upper North Street, Poplar, London

name: St Mary's Church, Battersea
description: During Open House, the Friends of Battersea Parish Church present a Floral Festival, organ recitals, historical displays, alongside 3 talks exploring history, creativity, sanctuary & Battersea’s radical past. Sat 12 Sept Dr. Peter Rumley at 6pm, Tues 15 Guy Stagg at 6.30pm,  Thurs 17 at 6.30pm Rory Walsh & Mike Squires.  Plus Join us for Choral Evensong amidst the flowers at St Mary’s Battersea.

name: St Michael's Chester Square
description: St Michael's Chester Square is a grade 2 listed church in the heart of Victoria, built in the late Decorated Gothic style. The War Memorial Chapel at the north east end of the church was designed by Giles Gilbert Scott and completed in 1920. The stained glass West Window is by Hugh Easton and two windows to the south are by Morris & Co and date to 1882.

name: St Michael's Church, Croydon
description: St Michael's is a Grade 1 listed building by architect J L Pearson. It was described by the poet John Betjeman as”one of Pearson’s loveliest churches” and Pevsner stated that “The interior is one of Pearson’s finest, and one of the most satisfying of its date anywhere”. There are particularly fine interior furnishings by eminent artists such as Bodley, Temple Moore and Comper.
address: St Michael's Church, Poplar Walk, Croydon, CR0 1UA

name: St Olave Hart Street
description: A Great Fire Survivor, damaged in the blitz, the post war restoration of this fascinating building began 75 years ago this year.  Described by John Betjeman as a 'country church in the world of Seething Lane' the building uniquely blends medieval fabric with Festival of Britain era motifs. Explore the medieval crypt, 'Pepys' vestry, church tower and ringing room. Bellringing demonstrations.

name: St Paul's, Newington
description: Modern architecture church with large copper and lead roof and concrete, brick and stained glass external structure. Marble, wood and plaster interior and artwork by Sculptor Freda Pinto and Gerald Holtom.

name: St Stephen's Church, Dulwich
description: Designed by Charles Barry Jr in the Victorian Gothic style, it has been a landmark in Dulwich since it was painted by the French Impressionist Camille Pissarro in 1870. There is a fine fresco painted by Sir Edward Poynter in the chancel.
address: St Stephen's Church, College Road, Dulwich, SE21 7HW

name: Stanley Arts
description:
First opened in 1903, Stanley Arts continues its building's legacy as a beacon for the local community. This Grade II listed Edwardian theatre, gallery, and public hall reflects its founder's interest in the arts and sciences.

The historic features of the building are sometimes hidden, other times flaunted. Our Open House tours cover everything past and present about this storied institution.

name: Suburban Art and Design in Petts Wood
description: Basil Scruby’s 1920’s-30’s classic Arts and Crafts style garden estate which was inspired by the character of the area’s woodland and rural open spaces. This guided walk of Petts Wood focuses on the contrasting house designs such as Tudor, Elizabethan and Art Deco including Charles Rene McIntosh influenced motifs. Stained glass also features at St Francis  church; a Nickolaus Pevsner listed historical building.
address: 36 Station Square, petts wood orpington, BR5 1NA

name: Suleymaniye Mosque
description: 6-storey building featuring a Western exterior and traditional Islamic interior, modelled on the Blue Mosque in Istanbul. Has dome and minaret tower.

name: Surbiton Queen of the Suburbs
description:
Join us for an interesting and informative walk around Surbiton with our experienced guide. Find out why Surbiton was called the Queen of the suburbs and plenty more. Learn about the Victorian churches of St Mark’s and St Andrews and see the mural of Rupert bear

Visit our website: https://www.kingstontourguides.org.uk/

name: Temple Bar
description: Temple Bar is a 350 year old gateway to the City of London, designed by Sir Christopher Wren. It formerly stood in Fleet Street, and is the last surviving gateway to the City of London. This beautiful structure has a fascinating history, which will be revealed to visitors.
address: First Floor, Paternoster Lodge, 2 Paternoster Square, EC4M 7DX

name: The Battle of Britain Bunker - The Generator House
description: Explore the Generator House at RAF Uxbridge’s Battle of Britain Bunker. Normally off‑limits to the public, it houses the original 1930s standby generator that powered the underground Operations Room coordinating RAF Fighter Command in WWII. It offers a glimpse into wartime engineering, featuring preserved machinery, original fittings, and fascinating stories.  Free admission, no booking required.

name: The Caledonian Club
description: Built in Neoclassical style for Hugh Morrison (1868-1931), this was the last mansion house of its kind to be built in London. The club, founded in 1891, moved to the premises in 1946.

name: The Dovecote, Eastcote House Gardens
description: The dovecote at Eastcote House Gardens is an 18th-century, Grade II listed brick structure with a tiled roof, originally built to house pigeons for food and manure. It replaced an earlier Elizabethan dovecote by the Hawtrey family. Now preserved as part of  a tranquil gardens. Usually out-of-bounds to the public, it reflects historic manor life.
address: Eastcote House Gardens, High Road, HA5 2FE

name: The Fleet beneath your feet
description: A walk along and around a stretch of London's most famous hidden river. The River Fleet is underground these days, but it's left its mark on the landscape. Discover the layers of history in this less explored corner of central London.

name: The Great Barn
description: Part of Manor Farm Heritage Site, The Great Barn is a Grade II listed  building and one of the oldest timber framed buildings of its type. Usually closed only for private events, the building as offers a glimpse into the rural history of the local area and is a testament to local craft and engineering.
address: Manor Farm, Bury Street / Eastcote Road, HA4 7SU

name: The Great Barn, Harmondsworth
description: This year we’re celebrating the 600th anniversary of Harmondsworth’s magnificent Great Barn. It’s over 190 feet long, nearly 40 feet high, and over 95% of its structural timbers are original. Displays include details of its construction, the conservation/repairs carried out in 2014, and its place in the agricultural history of the village.
address: Manor Court, High Street, Harmondsworth, UB7 0AQ

name: The Honourable Society of the Middle Temple
description: The Honourable Society of the Middle Temple is one of the four Inns of Court, exclusively entitled to Call their members to the Bar of England and Wales. We provide support, education and accomodation to barristers at every stage of their careers. Middle Temple Hall, Bench apartments, and Middle Temple Library will be open to the public on Sunday 13 September from 12-4pm. Last entry is at 3.45pm.
address: Middle Temple, Middle Temple Lane, London, EC4Y 9BT

name: The Ismaili Centre
description: Part of an international family of Ismaili Centres, this is a religious, cultural and social space for the Shia Imami Ismaili Muslims. The serenity of the entrance fountain to the roof garden reflects Muslim traditions in architecture and design.

name: The Manor House, Manor Farm, Ruislip
description: Manor Farm House in Ruislip, built in 1505–1507, is a Tudor-style, Grade II listed building that once hosted local court sessions and housed high-status guests. Now a visitor centre, it features original beams, historic displays, and forms part of the wider 22-acre Manor Farm heritage site.  It is also believed to be the home to the oldest example of surviving domestic English  wallpaper.
address: Manor Farm House, Eastocote Road, HA4 8BD

name: The South Wing
description: The South Wing is a design-led Victorian home, location house and creative space in Croydon, shaped by a belief that beauty, atmosphere and thoughtful detail can change how people feel. For Open House, visitors are invited inside a private residential space that explores home as stage, sanctuary and cultural invitation.

name: The St Michael Steiner School
description: Our school resides in a Grade II listed building on the edge of Hanworth Air Park. Fortescue House was the rectory for St. George's church on the edge of Hanworth Air Park. Later, it became a school, and now it is the home to the St. Michael Steiner School. We are blessed by beautiful grounds & woodland where the children can play & relax.  We enjoy the unique history and biodiversity of the area.
address: The St Michael Steiner School, Park Road, Hanworth, TW13 6PN

name: The Stanley Picker Trust, Picker House
description:
Completed in 1968 by Kenneth Wood, the house is an untouched time capsule of 1960s colour, innovation and design, with interiors  provided by the Conran Group. 

Situated in a quiet cul-de-sac on steeply sloping ground, the location was both an inspiration and a challenge for Ken Wood when creating the modern split-level design. The garden and pavilion gallery are also included in the tour.

name: The Temple Church
description: Medieval architecture meets Wren's refurbishments in this inspiring building, the Mother Church of the Common Law. The Magna Carta exhibit: has William Marshal and King John where they would have debated and agreed clauses of Magna Carta.

name: The Temple Wanstead Park
description: The Temple, 1760 remnant of the magnificent Wanstead House estate, set in Grade II landscape Wanstead Park, now woodland, grassland, lakes. Discover colourful Wanstead stories. New for 2026: finds from 18C grotto,

name: The Tin Tabernacle / Cambridge Hall
description: Constructed in 1863, Kilburn’s grade II corrugated Iron Church set about it’s new course in the 1950's when it’s interior was transformed to resemble naval training ship (TS) Bicester.

name: The Wallace Collection - Eranda Research Library
description: Built in 1776 for the Duke of Manchester to designs by John Crunden, Hertford House today holds the Wallace Collection. Join us in the Eranda Research Library to explore how an 18th century home developed into a world class museum. Discover our display of architectural drawings and prints, alongside items from the archive.
address: The Wallace Collection, Hertford House, Manchester Square, W1U 3BN

name: Timothy Hatton Architects – The Foundry
description:
Tucked behind a busy road in W12, this former foundry is a multi-level development featuring an architects’ studio with courtyards and spaces for exhibitions and musical performances. The  building's 15m brick chimney is a local landmark.

This year we have a new exhibition in our gallery, showcasing the work of celebrated British artist Sophie Smallhorn.

name: Tooting Bec Lido
description: Outdoor pool 100x33 yards. One million gallons of unheated water. Iconic outdoor cubicle doors, fountain and café added in the 1930s, with Art Deco style entrance in 2001. Sports hall pavilion added in 2016.
address: Tooting Bec Lido, Tooting Bec Road, SW16 1RU

name: Tower Hamlets Cemetery Park
description: One of the magnificent 7 cemeteries. Burials ceased 1966, now 31 acres of woodland, meadows & ponds including the Soanes Centre (Robson Kelly 1993). Of outstanding importance for flora and fauna, set amongst funereal monuments, some listed
address: Soanes Centre. (On the right the main gates on Southern Grove)

name: Trellick Tower
description: Goldfinger's 31-storey social housing tower is one of London's most remarkable high-rises. Monumental, with its free-standing service tower and triumphal boiler house, Trellick retains beautiful detailing and a rich use of materials.

name: Trinity Buoy Wharf/Container City
description:
Home to London's only lighthouse, fine stock buildings, examples of the innovative Container City buildings and SS Robin, the world’s only surviving complete
Victorian steamship. This former buoy manufacturing site is now a centre for the creative industries with various sculptures and installations.

name: Two Temple Place
description: Completed in 1895, Two Temple Place is a dazzling neo-Gothic gem on the Victoria Embankment, designed by gothic revivalist architect, John Loughborough Pearson, & commissioned by & built for William Waldorf Astor, as his estate office.

name: University of Greenwich, Stockwell Street
description: The building features a limestone exterior designed to 'complement but not mimic' the surrounding historical architecture, whilst behind the façade is a 4-storey composition of steel, glass and exposed concrete.

name: University of West London
description: The University of West London is offering guided tours of its Ealing site, led by some of our current students, offering the opportunity to discover more about the University’s history and how its facilities have been transformed in recent years.

name: Victorian artists at home in Kensington and Chelsea
description: This tour takes visitors around the haunts and homes of famous Victorian artists, both international and local, and explores the connections between these personalities and their work, the wider impact of their art on society then and now, and the excitement of the Victorian time period's prolific artistic output and invention.

name: W House
description:
W House is a fully refurbished and extended house in Fulham. Various interventions have been made to create better visual connections and improve the flow through the house. 

The new volume at the rear of the house has been inspired by a series of pre-fabricated moulding details found in a historical joinery catalogue from a local craftsman that operated in the area during the Victorian times.

name: Wade House
description: Turning what was once a backland site into a two-storey, two-bedroom detached home, Wade House introduces a modern new-build to the heart of Metroland.

name: Walk through the Stuart Dynasty and Cromwell’s Republic
description: Come and enjoy a circular 2-hour walk around Westminster, Whitehall and St James’ and hear about the events of one of the most tumultuous periods in London’s history, spanning the years 1603 (the death of Elizabeth I and arrival of James I), through Civil War, Regicide, Cromwell’s Republic, the Restoration right through to 1714 and the end of the Stuart Dynasty.
address: Meet outside Westminster Abbey Gift Shop, 20 Dean’s Yard, London

name: Walter Segal Self-build Houses
description: A close of 13 self-built houses. Each is unique, built using methods developed by Walter Segal, who led the project in the mid 1980s. Houses have been extended and renovated. Sustainable features including solar electric, water & space heating.
address: Walters Way, Honor Oak Park, SE23 3LH

name: Walthamstow Pumphouse Museum
description: Grade II listed Victorian engine house remodelled to take a pair of 1895 Marshall steam engines, still in working order. A museum celebrating the rich Industrial Heritage of the Borough and the Lea Valley Region.

name: Whose Paddington?
description: This walking tour uncovers the stories of urban redevelopment in Paddington, exploring how successive major infrastructure projects  have repeatedly reshaped the historic fabric of the area. We will trace the impact of these transformations, considering the balance between disruption and economic progress, asking who  benefited and who was left behind in their wake.
address: Warwick Avenue tube station, Street level, W9 2PT

name: Wimbledon Village Club, Museum and Lecture Hall
description: A Victorian Gothic Village Club and Lecture Hall comprising village hall, members’ club, museum, gallery and arts/ activities spaces.

name: Wimbledon Windmill Museum
description: Rare example of a hollow post mill (1817). Grade II* listed, it now contains a museum depicting the history and development of windmills in Britain. Many working models, windmill machinery, equipment and tools.

name: Wolves Lane Centre
description: This is a walking tour of the three acres, three new eco buildings and the eight glass houses on the Wolves Lane Centre site. This walking tour will include visiting the Palm House, with an abundance of exotic flora and fauna including lots of koi carp and terrapins, and the Cacti House which was started 18 years ago.

name: Wolves Lane Horticultural Centre
description: Ever explored an eco-building? Wolves Lane Horticulture centre is home to a thriving 3.5 acre contemporary community food growing space alongside 1970s glasshouses. Visit the cactus and palm house with koi carp alongside a “bale” of terrapins and exotic flora and fauna. The café serves healthy, locally grown produce and the shop will furnish you with plants to take home.
address: Wolves Lane Centre, Wolves Lane, N22 5JD

name: Wood House
description: An architect-designed home exploring modern methods of construction through an exposed cross-laminated timber (CLT) structure. Designed and self-built as a low-energy contemporary home, it showcases how traditional craftsmanship and innovative timber engineering can create sustainable, beautifully crafted living spaces.

name: Woodfield Pavilion
description: A pre-2nd WW - 1933 - now beautifully refurbished brick built sports pavilion surrounded by the fields of Tooting Common.
address: The Woodfield Pavilion,, Tooting Common, 16a Abbottswood Road

name: outhouse gallery
description:
outhouse gallery is a small, independent, artist-run creative space located in Brunswick Park, Camberwell. 
As a former public toilet, the gallery's mission is to be open, public and accessible to both facilitators and visitors - from free exhibitions, live performances, and workshops to publishing articles online and in outhouse magazine.
